fields.Name: Sales: Dashboard Summary
fields.UserQuestion: What are the dashboard headline figures for a period — won, commit, open pipeline, weighted pipeline and the forecast — and which open deals need attention?
fields.Description: The figures for the dashboard's tiles, forecast and Needs attention list, as one row, for an optional period and the filter bar's selling companies, product companies, owners and pipelines.
fields.TechnicalDescription: Grain: Deal, reduced to one row. Every count branches on a DealStatusType or ForecastCategoryType FLAG, never a name. PERIOD (bc-aidp-next-golive#350): PeriodStart/PeriodEnd bound Won (WonCount, WonAmount) on ActualCloseDate and every open figure (OpenAmount, OpenCount, OpenOmittedCount, CommitAmount, CommitCount, BestCaseOnlyAmount, PipelineOnlyAmount, WeightedAmount and the priced/stated split) on ExpectedCloseDate, through two flags in the scoped CTE; an open deal with no expected close date is in no bounded window, and NoCloseDateCount reports those whatever the period. PastExpectedCloseCount, NoOwnerCount and NoCloseDateCount are about today and ignore the period; PastExpectedCloseCount compares against the business day from __mj_BizAppsCommon.fnBusinessToday() (bc-aidp-next-golive#168). Omitting both period parameters is All time. FILTERS: CompanyIDs, OwnerEmployeeIDs, PipelineIDs and ProductCompanyIDs are arrays rendered with sqlIn and narrow every column; single-value CompanyID and PipelineID still work. ProductCompanyIDs keeps a deal when one line of its order (OrderLine.CompanyID) belongs to a selected company; the deal counts once at its full amount. NoLinesDealCount counts the deals in the other filters' scope whose order has no lines. Open deals in pipelines with IncludeInForecast = 0 are excluded unless PipelineID or PipelineIDs names the pipeline. Omitted forecast categories (IncludeInPipeline = 0) are left out of the money figures; OpenCount still counts them. CommitAmount + BestCaseOnlyAmount + PipelineOnlyAmount = OpenAmount. test-harnesses/compare-dashboard-measures.mjs recomputes every figure from deal rows under several periods and filters and fails on any disagreement.

_comments: NO EXPLICIT `relatedEntities` PARAMETERS, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
MJ's push path EXTRACTS query parameters from the Nunjucks template itself and inserts them. So
declaring the same names here too collides with what it just wrote:
Cannot insert duplicate key in object '__mj.QueryParameter'.
and the whole push aborts and rolls back. That is the same failure the other thirteen query files
hit on a RE-push -- they carry explicit parameter rows, which land once on a clean database and
then collide with themselves forever after. Leaving parameters to extraction makes this file
idempotent: pushing it twice is a no-op rather than a rollback.
The cost is that the generated parameter descriptions are heuristic rather than hand-written (MJ
tries an LLM first and falls back when no model credentials are configured). Worth it here: a
parameter called CompanyID on a query called Sales: Dashboard Summary is not the part a reader
struggles with, and the TechnicalDescription below carries the reasoning that actually matters.

Former description, kept as the design note: The four KPI tiles as a single row of scalars. Added because the other thirteen queries do not answer them as scalars: Pipeline Summary is grouped by stage and open-only, Deal Roster carries the past-close flag per row, and Bookings by Period is date-windowed — composing the tiles from those would have moved the SQL to the server and left the aggregation in the browser, which is the half §9.5 is about. Also returns the priced/stated split of the open figure so a tile can say how much of it nobody priced. WonCount accepts an optional period window; the other figures never do.
